test_title: PYST 12 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. He has been B. to Italy, C. but he D. didn't went to Rome.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the past tense verb "**went**" following the auxiliary verb "**didn't**" (did not).
 
• In English grammar, when using the auxiliary verb "do," "does," or "did" for negation or questions, the main verb must always be in its **base form** (infinitive without "to").
 
• The auxiliary "did" already indicates the past tense, so using "went" creates an incorrect double-past construction.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part D** (Option 4) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He has been to Italy, but he **didn't go** to Rome."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "He has been"** – This uses the present perfect tense correctly to describe a life experience (visiting Italy).
 
• **B: "to Italy,"** – The preposition "to" is correctly used after "been" to indicate direction or destination.
 
• **C: "but he"** – This uses the coordinating conjunction "but" correctly to introduce a contrasting idea.
 
• **Verb Base Form:** Common examples of this rule include: *"He didn't **know**"* (not *knew*), *"She didn't **see**"* (not *saw*), and *"They didn't **come**"* (not *came*).
